description: Comb filter bank: 64 taps spread across one delay length by pattern, in stereo, with feedback.

params.text: Sets the comb length as a division of the clock, in 21 steps from a single clock period to 256 of them, taking in thirds, fifths, sevenths and elevenths on the way.
Sets the comb length directly, from 1ms to 10 seconds, starting at 350ms; a cable in the clock input takes over from this knob.
Chooses one of 16 patterns for how the 64 taps are spaced across the comb length; the last eight are randomly perturbed versions of the first eight.
Sets how many of the 64 taps sound, from 1 to 64; the silenced ones are spread through the pattern rather than cut from the end.
Sets the level of the first and last taps, with the levels in between sloping towards the tent tap.
Sets the level at the tent tap, with the levels sloping away from it to the edge level at both ends.
Chooses which tap, from 1 to 63, is the peak of the level slope.
Chooses the feedback shaping: Guitar averages each pass with the one before, Sitar does that and stretches the delay by up to 10% with input level, Clarinet soft-clips, Raw shapes nothing.
Sets how much of the delayed signal returns to the input, from none to all of it.

inputs.text: Times the comb length from the interval between two triggers, and takes over from the SIZE knob while patched.
Moves the clock division by about two of its 21 steps per volt.
Shortens or lengthens the comb by a volt per octave, working from either the clock or the SIZE knob.
Adds to the comb length at 1 second per volt, and does nothing while a clock is patched.
Moves the comb pattern by one and a half patterns per volt.
Moves the tap count by 6.4 taps per volt.
Moves the edge level, 10V covering its whole range.
Moves the tent level, 10V covering its whole range.
Moves the tent tap by 6.3 taps per volt.
Moves the feedback type by one step per 10V.
Moves the feedback amount, 10V covering its whole range.
The left input to the comb, which feeds both sides when the right input is empty.
The right input to the comb; with nothing patched here, the left input feeds both sides.

outputs.text: The left comb output, the sounding taps summed with no dry signal in them.
The right comb output, the sounding taps summed with no dry signal in them.
The comb length as a voltage, at one volt per second.

notes: patching a clock into the clock input takes the comb length from that clock and the division, and the SIZE knob stops being read.

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
